name: Discovery: first look around the host
summary: Read-only discovery an intruder typically runs right after landing on a host: who am I, what is this machine, what is on the network, who else has accounts here. Nothing is created or changed.
objectives: Find the burst of discovery commands and the process that launched them.
List which ATT&CK discovery techniques were used, in order.
Explain why a short burst of built-in tools from one parent is suspicious.

steps.title: Current user and privileges (whoami /all)
expected_detections: whoami.exe with /all from a script host or shell
hunt_notes: Start from whoami.exe on {{Host}} in this step's UTC window; its parent is the start of the discovery burst.

steps.title: System information (systeminfo)
expected_detections: systeminfo.exe executed shortly after other discovery
hunt_notes: systeminfo.exe and reg.exe query from the same parent as whoami.exe.

steps.title: Network configuration (ipconfig, arp, nbtstat, net config)
expected_detections: Several network discovery tools run in quick succession
hunt_notes: ipconfig.exe, netsh.exe, arp.exe, nbtstat.exe and net.exe within seconds of each other.

steps.title: Running processes (tasklist)
hunt_notes: tasklist.exe: often used to look for security tools.

steps.title: Local accounts (net user, cmdkey /list)
hunt_notes: net.exe user, cmdkey.exe /list (stored credentials) and a dir of C:\Users.

steps.title: Local groups and administrators (net localgroup)
expected_detections: Enumeration of the local Administrators group
hunt_notes: net.exe localgroup "Administrators": who could the intruder target for privilege escalation?

steps.title: Network connections and sessions (netstat, net use)
Network shares on this host (net view)
hunt_notes: net.exe view \\localhost closes the burst. Build the full timeline from whoami.exe to here.
